ateret-zekenim/1:_: And infants of the beit rabban, etc. And even bad words are likewise forbidden to learn with them, because the infants do not understand well what they utter from their mouths, and their principal joy is in knowing what they are saying; therefore one may not distinguish between them regarding words of comfort versus bad things; therefore if the infant understands what he is saying, it is permitted to learn bad things with him. There is one who wrote that one should not bless on Tisha B'Av and Yom Kippur "who has provided all my needs," because then it is forbidden to wear sandals [Lechem Min HaShamayim]; and if he must go before the minister and they are strict about him if he goes without shoes, he should put dust in his shoes and walk (Mordechai end of Moed Katan). And wherever it is necessary to walk in shoes, he should do so. And the custom that women wash their heads from minchah onward — and the early elders instituted this and made support for the matter based on what was said in the aggadah that the Messiah was born on Tisha B'Av — and one must make a remembrance of the redeemer and comfort them so they do not despair of redemption; and this is specifically for women, because they are weak in believing consolations since they do not know Scripture; therefore they need strengthening (Kol Bo). And commerce — if it is a lost matter, it is permitted as they permitted on the festivals (Rashba responsa siman 591). And any melacha — even that of a layman, even if it is not laborious — if there is something in it that he derives some amusement from it, one should not do it on Tisha B'Av, for thereby he nullifies the affliction (Terumat HaDeshen siman 153).
baer-heitev/16:_: Forbidden. The Taz wrote all the more so one must forbid for those who have gaiters of leather — that is, both what is on the legs of leather, and also those that are of cloth, only that the edges are of leather are forbidden, end of his words. And the Bach is stricter to go completely barefoot. And even though it is forbidden on Tisha B'Av to wear sandals, nevertheless they bless "who has provided all my needs," and the Arizal ruled not to bless.
beer-hagolah/4:_: Tur in the name of the Ramban
beer-hagolah/6:_: Tur in the name of the Rambam, and the same law, and so it appears
beer-hagolah/11:א: Tur in the name of the Yerushalmi as per his textual reading and his explanation
beer-hagolah/14:_: Tur in the name of the Yerushalmi there
beer-hagolah/19:_: Tur in the name of his father the Rosh from the language of the Tosefta, and so wrote the Ramban
beur-hagra/11:_: After it has been wiped dry, etc. Yerushalmi chapter 1 of Taanis halachah 6: as on the public fast days one washes his face, hands, and feet in his usual manner; on Tisha B'Av one washes his hands and passes over his face; and the Tur's textual reading is "over his eyes," and he explained it in this manner. And they said there, in Yom Kippur — one washes his hands and wipes with a cloth and passes the cloth over his face — meaning like a kind of dried vessels; and from this there is proof that washing hands is permitted on Tisha B'Av and Yom Kippur.
beur-hagra/22:ב: And they did not practice, etc. — as on the public fast days until "you shall be humbled," etc. And Ran chapter 4 of Pesachim, and as I wrote siman 555 seif 1, see there.
beur-hagra/22:ג: And they practice to be strict, etc. — for the reason of the prohibition of melacha is that through melacha he will forget the sorrow and fasting, and as I wrote above — Rashbag says a person should always make himself like a Torah scholar so that he will fast; and this is specifically regarding melacha that involves delay.
beur-hagra/22:ד: And to milk, etc. — for it is in doubt in Terumat HaDeshen and in Magen Avraham; but Rashba wrote that a lost matter is permitted, and likewise below in seif 23; and as I wrote in Terumat HaDeshen that certainly the voice of Tisha B'Av protests against it, and furthermore that the prohibition is only custom.
beur-hagra/22:ה: If possible. — for in this manner even a mourner it is permitted, as I wrote in the end of chapter 8 of Moed Katan — that is to say, etc., and likewise here through a non-Jew.
biur-halacha/1:_: It is void — the Taz wrote that the prohibition regarding infants is not because they are joyful, for they certainly have no joy, but because of the teacher who rejoices in words of Torah when he studies with them, end of his words; and he comes to exclude the view of the Bach; and from Magen Avraham it is implied that he agrees with the Bach that they have joy. And know that per Taz, when the infants study by themselves there is no prohibition; however in truth the language of the Gemara and Teshuvos HaRashba "are void in it" implies that they are completely idle, and in particular when the child is between twelve years old, somewhat grown and understands — even the Taz concedes that it is forbidden to study independently, not in bad matters, because it is joy for him, as the Peri Megadim wrote.
biur-halacha/6:_: In a place of illness, etc. — see in the book Pitchei Olam that in a place where cholera is not prevalent, Heaven forbid, he should eat less than a kotevet within the time of eating a peras, and likewise for drinking per the measures in Shulchan Aruch siman 618 (thus one should instruct a questioner on Tisha B'Av that by this the fast is not completely uprooted, and the Merciful One desires the heart); and one who wishes to fast in a place where the illness is not in wrath, Heaven forbid, should be advised and warned not to go from the threshold of his house all day, and when he goes out he should carry around his nose and mouth a piece of camphor and a bit of mint grass, end of his words.
chatam-sofer/18:_: Seif 18 in the gloss: and some say marital relations — see responsa Ketav Sofer siman 101.
chatam-sofer/3:_: Note: as the words of the Bach are explained explicitly in the language of the Rambam and in Torat Adam to the Ramban page 86 end of 13a, that it is forbidden only for the public fast days, see there.
eliyah-rabbah/1:_: [1] [Levush] And even to lie down, etc. And it is possible that it is forbidden to touch it as on Yom Kippur (Darkei Moshe), and it appears to me that one may be lenient by day (Magen Avraham), and study is required — for at the end of siman 615 he forbids even by day if it is reasonable for him to distinguish between Yom Kippur and Tisha B'Av in this; if so, whence does he have to distinguish to study at night from Yom Kippur? However, the Taz there permits touching on Tisha B'Av entirely, since she goes about in soiled garments and will not desire it so much; also from the reason of the Levush there because of keri it is implied that on Tisha B'Av it is permitted; nevertheless it is good to be strict.
eliyah-rabbah/7:_: [7] An animal every thirty days, etc. See what the Taz challenged on Rashal from siman 618 on Yom Kippur; and in my humble opinion it is not difficult at all, for Rashal deals explicitly with an animal that must fast on Yom Kippur after seven days even though it said "I need," as was explained in siman 617; but regarding an ill person he deals even though it does not say "I need," and he says that estimation is not required.
eliyah-rabbah/11:_: [11] [Levush] Until it is dried, etc. — until there is not enough moisture on it to moisten something else (Bach and Magen Avraham). To remove filth, etc. — in the Tur that one does now for pleasure is permitted.
eliyah-rabbah/18:_: [18] When Tisha B'Av falls on Shabbos, etc. It appears to say Av Harachamim — even though Tisha B'Av is called a festival, nevertheless Av Harachamim is like kinot that are recited on Tisha B'Av; see the end of siman 484. And furthermore, for even in Tachanun and Tziduk HaDin the Taz wrote siman 599 that one should say it on Tisha B'Av even though they do not practice thus; nevertheless do not add, since it was not mentioned by the poskim; and the Taz already wrote there seif katan 5 that it is permitted to deliver a eulogy on Tisha B'Av, and this is his language: "Magalei Tzedek mentions the souls of the earlier rabbis and the communities killed for the sanctity of the Name and Av Harachamim," until here; and it is implied also on Tisha B'Av on Shabbos.
kaf-hachayyim/1:_: (1) [Seif 1] Tisha B'Av is forbidden in bathing, etc. And everything the Sages forbade is forbidden until night, such as eating and drinking; except things that are only custom not mentioned in the Talmud, such as sitting on the ground — in this some practice to be lenient after noon. Shlah page 199b. And likewise the Bach siman 599. And Rosh Chodesh wrote: let one who does one of all these all day be in excommunication. And Beit Din Hatnia and She'ilat Ya'avetz. Magen Avraham seif katan 1. Eliyah Rabbah seif 2. However those who go among the gentiles and engage in commerce after noon — they are permitted to wear shoes, and from them everyone learned to be lenient, and one should protest against them. Magen Avraham there. Eliyah Rabbah there. Mishna Berurah seif 1; and see below seif 5.
kaf-hachayyim/4:_: (4) And nevertheless it is permitted to inhale tobacco through the nostrils on Tisha B'Av and Yom Kippur; but one who practices the prohibition stands in his prohibition and one may not permit him, as written above siman 210 seif 37, see there. And those who place good fragrance in powder on Tisha B'Av do not do well. Malach siman 10 seif 14. And see below siman 556 regarding good fragrance and perfumes.
kaf-hachayyim/7:_: (7) There. And it is forbidden to read from the Torah, etc. — one who undertook to ascend to the Torah on Tisha B'Av and it happened that he is a mourner may ascend to the Torah on the morning of Tisha B'Av, since it is bad matters, and everyone is forbidden in Torah like him. Beit Yehuda volume 2 siman 84. And it is simple that certainly he may ascend to the Torah in the morning and read the haftarah even though he is a mourner. Machatzit HaShekel seif 1. And Beit Din HaSh'at seif 1. And he wrote and it is implied that even if he did not undertake to ascend to the Torah on Tisha B'Av the law is likewise. And see below siman 599 seif 55.
kaf-hachayyim/14:_: (14) There. And the chapter "These may shave." And even though it contains several laws of nidui and cherem, it is permitted to study; but certainly to carry and give before a Torah scholar — since the matter is publicized greatly, it is possibly forbidden. Responsa Maharil siman 201. And Beit Din Beit Yosef. Magen Avraham seif katan 4. And likewise the Taz seif katan 2 that even in a place where study is permitted — that is, that he should study in the plain sense of matters, but not through pilpul; and even in thought to explain a difficult matter is forbidden because he will have joy after he settles himself, end of his words. And Beit Din Mishna Berurah seif 4; and see further below seif 15.
kaf-hachayyim/22:_: (22) There, gloss. And it is permitted to review the parasha, etc. It appears that this is what he said — one who is accustomed to review the parasha (Shemot LeVush) on that day — that is, when Tisha B'Av falls on Thursday it is like the order of the day. Taz seif katan 3. And such is the view of Eliyah Rabbah seif 7. And likewise Mahara Azulai wrote in his glosses on Kol Yehudah from there Magen Avraham; only that he disagreed with him and wrote that it is not fitting to be lenient in this. And Beit Din Birkei Yosef seif 3. And likewise Chida seif 3 on the words of the Taz mentioned that there is great strain to explain thus. And likewise Nahar Shalom on the words of the Taz mentioned that it is very difficult to be lenient in this. And Mishna Berurah seif katan 8 wrote to explain the words of Nahar Shalom mentioned — that is, the chazan who reads is permitted to review the parasha before he reads; or it deals with Tisha B'Av that falls on Shabbos, for then even an individual is permitted to review the parasha, as I wrote above siman 485, end of his words. However Eliyah Rabbah there challenged the words of Magen Avraham mentioned, for behold "when you bear children" is of the type of the event. And Nahar Shalom there wrote: it is possible that Magen Avraham on the parasha "and he began" speaks — they practiced to read it at minchah as on the other public fast days; but the parasha "when you bear" and the like — for everyone it is permitted, see there. And Machatzit HaShekel wrote to reconcile that also in "when you bear" it could be that there is joy in what one learns the cantillation and vowels by heart — it teaches us that it is permitted, for there is not so much joy for the chazan in this, see there. And such is the view of the later authorities per the words of Magen Avraham mentioned.
kaf-hachayyim/24:_: (24) There. As the manner that they fast and make restitution on Yom Kippur — except that this is karet punishment and that is from words of Kabbalah, and prepares him for makkat mardut. Tur. Levush in seif 4; and see above siman 496 seif 11 and siman 468 seif 6.
levushei-serad/5:_: There. And see siman 593 — meaning that the Rama forbids to study on Tisha B'Av when it happens to be on Shabbos; therefore it teaches us here that reviewing the parasha is the order of the day and permitted. Not like those who permit study — there is no need to inform us at all.
levushei-serad/6:_: Taz seif katan 3. It appears that this is what he said. It was difficult for him — for behold the essence of the mitzvah to review the parasha of Shemot is on erev Shabbos, and Tisha B'Av does not fall on erev Shabbos; therefore he explained "one whose way is to review Shemot on Thursday" — because he is occupied on erev Shabbos with Shabbos needs. And Magen Avraham in seif katan 7 explained in another way; and see responsa Arba Turim Even siman 11.
machatzit-hashekel/2:_: (Seif katan 2) And infants, etc. — even though he does not understand, etc.; if so, regarding the infant good and bad things are one; nevertheless he rejoices in what he knows to read and say — explaining the words even though he does not know the content of the matter. And therefore, etc., with others as written in Yoreh De'ah. And if so, with an infant — whether he understands or does not understand — it is forbidden; and even bad matters from the prohibition of the teacher. However according to what is written in Yoreh De'ah there — if many need him, it is permitted. And Shach wrote that a teacher of infants is considered like many, it must be so. And also the Taz who did not lighten except after three days before — from this Magen Avraham understood siman 599 seif katan 8 that Tisha B'Av is called after three days. And perhaps since here on Tisha B'Av the mourning applies also to the minor who has reached education, it is stricter; and the Taz wrote here that all study with the infant is not because of the infant, for the infant is not joyful in his learning, and the prohibition is only because of the teacher. And if so, even an infant who does not understand is forbidden. And this is specifically what is not bad matters.
machatzit-hashekel/5:_: (Seif katan 5) Through thought, etc. — for ruling is like thought, as I wrote siman 485. That the Rama wrote siman 6 end of siman 6, and these are his words: and in a place where it is permitted to think in words of Torah, it is permitted to rule law, etc., end of his words — behold he equated them.
machatzit-hashekel/9:ג: (3) And see there, in Shulchan Aruch, etc. — meaning from that place itself that he proved in Darkei Moshe from the long composition of Rabbeinu Yerucham that she shall fast is proven from the words of Rabbeinu Yerucham in Shulchan Aruch that she shall not fast. He wrote in siman 599 seif 7: if the woman in labor recited the blessing at the circumcision and heard the blessing, she drinks — even if the circumcision is on the eighth day; and the same law after seven days. For behold if we give seven days we do not require from time to time, but per his reasoning it could be said that in Shulchan Aruch he retracted from what he said in his long composition, for we find thus in other places; but also his words in Shulchan Aruch contradict this — in Yoreh De'ah siman 265 seif 4 Rabbeinu Yerucham wrote, and these are his words: on the three fasts the woman in labor does not fast — one says the blessing over the cup, etc.; but on Yom Kippur and Tisha B'Av, when the woman in labor cannot drink, one does not bless over the cup, end of his words — behold he wrote that on Tisha B'Av she fasts.
machatzit-hashekel/9:ד: (4) Therefore the Bach explained what is written in Yoreh De'ah and likewise here in his long composition he wrote per the custom, and as the Rama wrote that they practice to fast, etc.; see Bach siman 599. And likewise the Taz in Yoreh De'ah there; but for the law Rabbeinu Yerucham holds that she need not fast, as is written here.
machatzit-hashekel/20:_: (Seif katan 20) And some say, etc. — and he ruled Shlah, etc. (Essay 8) that Shlah wrote in the gate of the letters, letter kuf. Meaning that he wrote in seif 8 that in this era there is no immersion at its time and there is no mitzvah; nevertheless behold Rabbeinu Yerucham in Yoreh De'ah — when her husband is in the city, even in this era there is a mitzvah. For Yehoshua was punished and did not leave a son, since he nullified Israel one night from marital relations, as stated at the beginning of Megillah (and it should be for Shlah that they are stricter regarding the night of immersion more than other mitzvah of marital relations — for on the night of immersion there is more concern for nullifying marital relations, for a woman conceives only close to her immersion; therefore if the night of her immersion did not occur on Shabbos he did not rely to permit marital relations so much in Avot of R' Natan). If so, since Rabbeinu Yerucham considered immersion a mitzvah when her husband is in the city — therefore marital relations then is an important mitzvah; and meaning when Tisha B'Av falls on a weekday they did not permit marital relations even on the night of immersion, for it is fitting that the house of our God be nullified for it one immersion (as R' Chiya the deputy high priest said, chapter 1 of Taanis); but when it falls on Shabbos, since in any case most poskim permit marital relations for a great mitzvah, he relied on the permissive view. However in Avot of R' Natan he wrote in the name of his elder likewise Mahararash that it is forbidden on erev Shabbos.
machatzit-hashekel/22:_: (Seif katan 22) To his fellow — he explained Torah scholar is missing, and so it should be in the Tur: there is no inquiry of peace to fellows on Tisha B'Av, and laymen who do not know, etc.; and the Bach explained (from that it teaches "fellows" and not "fellow") that it means Torah scholars who are called fellows. (And per this it is implied that laymen are permitted, as with melacha in seif 22.) And we do not know from where, etc. — meaning that "fellows" that the Tur wrote means Torah scholar; nevertheless he did not come to exclude that laymen are permitted. Rather he comes to teach that if one inquired of his wellbeing that he must respond in soft language. And regarding a Torah scholar you do not find this, for both of them know there is a prohibition in inquiring of peace; therefore he wrote there is no inquiry of peace to fellows, and they both know; but laymen who do not know — if it happened that a layman inquired of the peace of a Torah scholar, he responds to him in soft language.
machatzit-hashekel/23:ד: (4) And in my humble opinion for the public fast days as Rashba holds in tractate Taanis mentioned, to compare them. As stated in the Gemara Taanis daf 12b that explains regarding that they forbade on a fast washing, anointing, marital relations, melacha — granted all these have pleasure in them, but melacha is affliction. R' Chiya, R' Yosi bar Avin said: sanctify the fast, call an assembly, gather the elders. Just as on a festival melacha is forbidden, so too on a fast melacha is forbidden. If as on a festival — also at night; so too a fast, even at night. R' Zeira, etc. — gather the elders: just as gathering elders is by day, so too a fast also by day. And Rashi explained gathering elders by day — for at night each is in his house and they are not gathered, end of his words.
machatzit-hashekel/25:ב: (2) But in some poskim it is implied, etc. — and likewise he proved in Terumat HaDeshen there and challenges Rashi that nullifying melacha is affliction. Behold on the contrary on daf 12b the Talmud calls doing melacha affliction, brought above seif katan 23, see there. And it must be understood how Terumat HaDeshen understood the words of Rashbag who said "so that he will fast" without Rashi's explanation. For if doing melacha is affliction, what is "so that he will fast"? Therefore it must be that he explained as I wrote in seif katan 23 — that they not distract their minds from affliction, for through doing melacha he will distract his mind from mourning and affliction and will not fast. Not so through nullifying melacha — they will be afflicted through the afflictions forbidden to him, for he will not distract his mind from them. And it must be that Terumat HaDeshen holds that for this reason it would have been fitting to permit melacha that is not laborious and the act of a layman — for such melacha is not distraction of mind. Also what he concluded that likewise the reason is because of prohibition of melacha — meaning not from the aspect that it is affliction; but nevertheless the reason that melacha is forbidden in itself like Yom Kippur (even though he equated it in responsa to Yom Kippur, nevertheless they are not equal in their reasons) — rather on Tisha B'Av the reason is lest he distract his mind, for otherwise the statement of Rashbag "so that he will fast" is difficult as above; and if so it must be what Magen Avraham wrote in seif katan 23 and Terumat HaDeshen pilpul to find a reason — for also Terumat HaDeshen holds this reason.
magen-avraham/4:א: (1) It is permitted to read, etc. In Pozna they practice not to recite Tehillim and Shir HaYichud except on the morrow — of last night and of today (Levush); and in this country they practice to say them at minchah even though words of Torah are forbidden all day — it must be that he holds since he says them as a manner of supplication, it is permitted to say them at minchah; and for this reason they are lenient regarding tefillin at minchah.
magen-avraham/20:ב: (2) To his fellow. (In the Tur it is written "to my fellows") — he explained Torah scholars do not give peace to one another; but in Mordechai he wrote "to his fellow" — implying whoever is his fellow, even if not a Torah scholar, is forbidden (Bach); and we do not know what he is saying, for certainly it is forbidden to give peace to any person; but regarding laymen who do not know — when they give peace, they respond to them in soft language.
magen-avraham/22:א: (1) Not to do — so that they not distract their minds from mourning (Ra'avad chapter 4 of Pesachim). And in Terumat HaDeshen he pilpul to find a reason as written nearby; and it appears to me for this reason melacha is also forbidden at night (for at night too one is obligated to mourn); and likewise Rashi on Pesachim daf 54b — between his suns it is forbidden in eating and melacha; and study is required — for in Taanis daf 13 Rashi from here implies that on the night of Tisha B'Av they are permitted in melacha and the prohibition is only by day, and they do not publicize the matter, end of his words; and from the conclusion of all poskim it is implied that it is forbidden also at night. And in my humble opinion for the public fast days — there the reason is that they be free and gather to pray (see siman 575 seif 3); therefore they are permitted at night, for they did not gather at night, as stated in the Gemara; not so on Tisha B'Av where melacha is not forbidden and it depends on their custom — they practice prohibition; their reason is lest they distract their minds from mourning, or because of affliction; therefore also at night it is forbidden; therefore any melacha that has no delay is permitted, for he does not distract his mind thereby, as above.
mishnah-berurah/1:א: (1) It is forbidden in bathing, etc., and it is forbidden to read from the Torah, etc. — and all these things are forbidden all day, even during twilight until the stars emerge; and praying ma'ariv early does not help for this. However those who go among the gentiles and engage in commerce after noon — they are permitted to wear shoes [and see below in seif 17 in the gloss and in Mishna Berurah]; and from them everyone learned to be lenient, and one should protest against them.
mishnah-berurah/2:ב: (4) May shave — even though it also contains several laws of nidui and cherem, nevertheless study is permitted; but to carry and give in halachah is certainly forbidden [Magen Avraham in the name of Maharil]. And likewise the Taz wrote that even in a place where study is permitted — that is, he should study in the plain sense of matters, but not through pilpul; and even in thought to explain a difficult matter is forbidden because he will have joy after he settles himself.
mishnah-berurah/4:ב: (7) And the section of sacrifices and mishnah, etc. — for all this is no less than what they read from the Torah and read haftarah from the prophets; and all because it is the order of the day, and they practice to say Tehillim and Shir HaYichud at minchah even though words of Torah are forbidden all day — it must be that he holds since it is a manner of supplication it is permitted. And in Pozna they practice to say it on the morrow of last night and of today; and such is correct. And Ma'amadot — certainly one should not say; and see below siman 599 seif 4 that one should not say Pitum HaKetoret that is not of the order of the day; and all the more one should not say the order of sacrifices written at the end of seif 1; and what is written in Shulchan Aruch "and the section of sacrifices" means the section of the daily offering.
mishnah-berurah/19:ב: (40) And likewise they practice — and the shamash announces things done in private as practiced. However if the night of her immersion occurred on this Shabbos — this brought Magen Avraham in the name of Shlah that one may rely on this on the first view and she immerses and has marital relations; and some are strict also in this; and see in Chayei Adam who wrote that since on the night of immersion it is a mitzvah of marital relations, one may rely on this on the permissive view; and the Rama wrote they practice prohibition — meaning in a place where there is no mitzvah of marital relations here; not so on the night of immersion erev, in my humble opinion; and see in Biur HaGra that it is implied from him too that he sides with the halachah per the Mechaber's view; and if so one may rely to be lenient at least on the night of immersion.
mishnah-berurah/22:ב: (44) Does — and it does not appear like presumption, for the viewer says his refraining from melacha is because it did not happen for him — what is there to do.
peri-megadim/1:_: And infants — the Taz wrote this to exclude the view of the Bach; and from Magen Avraham seif 2 it appears that a child twelve years old, somewhat grown and understanding — even the Taz concedes it is forbidden to study independently what is joy for him; and specifically a small one who has distress in his study, etc. And see siman 591 in Magen Avraham letter 38. Eliyah Rabbah and Eliyah Zuta that words of Torah are forbidden all day until emergence of stars — everything forbidden by law; and specifically sitting on benches that is custom — permitted after noon. See Tur: one who eats and drinks receives makkat mardut; and study is required whether for other afflictions he receives; and study is required if he ate during twilight whether he receives also at nightfall — see responsa Razd in the practice of Iza and Shibuta in Beit Yosef that one does not lash makkat mardut on doubt; and in Shoshanas HaAmakim in the category of makkat mardut we wrote from this; and there is a difference for disqualification of testimony — Rambam chapter ten of Laws of Testimony: the obligation in it is from their words, end of his words, siman 34; see in Rambam Laws of chametz and Matzah chapter 1 halachah 7 what he wrote regarding Pesach — nevertheless it is implied in six no; and in halachah 10 "enjoys" implies no lashing; nevertheless the rule is implied: all these if not, likewise no lashing; likewise rabbinically yes; and on this end of his words there. And study is required; and in Sefer Shalah we wrote this at length.
peri-megadim/6:_: And likewise the Taz and Beit Yosef; and in siman 613 in the laws of Yom Kippur; and in the Taz there letter 6 — a rabbinic doubt where there is no washing of pleasure; and there the rabbi is forbidden with the student, and the same law here the rabbi with the student; and Magen Avraham there and Beit Yosef here, see there; and see Levush on this.
peri-megadim/9:_: Permitted — the Taz; and see siman 593 letter 2; and immersion at its time on Tisha B'Av on Shabbos — Magen Avraham wrote that poskim in the name of Shlah permit; and Eliyah Rabbah seif 19 implies that he forbids to have relations with her; and this will be explained in Magen Avraham: Tisha B'Av when it falls on Shabbos — Eliyah Rabbah seif 11 wrote that one says Av Harachamim, for it is like kinot; and they mention the souls of the righteous; and in siman 599 letter 6 the Taz that it is permitted to deliver a eulogy on Tisha B'Av for a Torah scholar; and the same law for Av Harachamim.
shaarei-teshuvah/1:_: In Shulchan Aruch: And it is forbidden to read from the Torah, etc. And Machatzit HaShekel wrote in the name of Beit Yehuda volume 2: one who undertook to ascend to the Torah on Tisha B'Av and became a mourner — he is permitted to ascend to the Torah in the morning, since it is bad matters and everyone is forbidden in Torah like him, see there. And Machatzit HaShekel wrote that it is simple he may ascend to the Torah and read haftarah; and it is implied that even if he did not undertake to ascend to the Torah on Tisha B'Av the law is likewise.
shaarei-teshuvah/8:_: Immersion — Be'er Heitev: see Mahari Bruna in the name of Zera Emet — if it happened that she did not bathe and did chafifah on Tisha B'Av, b'dieved one should permit her to bathe and do chafifah at the conclusion of Tisha B'Av; and see there; and see in responsa at the end of the book Mishnat R' Eliezer on daf 91, 14; and I was amazed at what he mocked the Be'er Heitev — how did he not see in Magen Avraham that Be'er Heitev did not innovate anything, only copied it in the letter of Magen Avraham's words; and what he wrote "and see siman 591," etc. — meaning that there it is explained that specifically if it is impossible at the conclusion of Tisha B'Av, and he did not come to dispute but to explain; and the disputing rabbi did not pay attention to him that it is so in Magen Avraham, only at the end he mentions from Magen Avraham's words to learn from him that chafifah is permitted on Tisha B'Av in all respects; and in my humble opinion Magen Avraham's intent was to show a place for the Rama as written; and see there that for the law his view is that even l'chatchila she should do chafifah on Tisha B'Av and at the conclusion of Tisha B'Av do chafifah a little (and then she must be careful not to go completely barefoot lest mud and mire stick to her, as Levush wrote, if she wishes to practice like the Rama — when possible to do chafifah at the conclusion of Tisha B'Av, command the woman to stay one hour in the business of chafifah and she fulfills all views of Rashi and Tosafos; and thus it is fitting to instruct, see there).
yad-ephraim/2:_: In the Taz seif katan 4 — and it is difficult, for from that he said "estimation is not required" it is implied there is doubt, etc.; and apparently his words are difficult to understand, for in his answer he concludes that it means estimation is not required — even certainly there is no danger in it, etc. Also study is required — what compelled him in his answer to explain even certainly there is no danger, etc., and not explain this "estimation is not required" simply — that it deals with doubt, but that she did not say "I need"; and it appears his intent: the Taz thus challenged — from that he said "she does not require estimation" it is implied it deals with an ill person where we are in doubt whether there is danger in the matter; and he says estimation is not required — perhaps according to my assessment she will be endangered because of the fast; rather they feed her immediately. And this was difficult for the Taz — for if she says "I need," if so what does it teach us that estimation is not required? For behold even if physicians assess her and say there is no danger, nevertheless if a physician says she does not need and the ill person says she needs — we heed the ill person. And what the Taz wrote "there is no danger" — estimation does not apply; one could say if it deals with an ill person where danger does not apply and there is no doubt in the matter that certainly there is no place for danger — if so estimation does not apply; and therefore it must deal where there is doubt whether she will be endangered; if so it is obvious that estimation is not required — for even if they assessed her we pay no attention, since estimation is required; and also one should not explain "estimation is not required" simply and she did not say "I need" — for then it would be truly difficult, since then they would assess her that there is no danger in her it would be forbidden; if so what difference to me Yom Kippur that is d'oraisa, what to me Tisha B'Av that is d'rabbanan — why should we not assess her? And if they say she will not be endangered we should not feed her, since she does not say "needs"; and likewise for an ill person in this manner — for if we knew there is no danger we would not feed her. One may not be lenient without assessment; therefore the Taz explained that it means estimation is not required — meaning that even if they assess that she will not be endangered, nevertheless they feed her even though she does not say "needs," since this ill person in any event there is doubt lest she be endangered through it; we have no need to be strict per the assessment that she will not be endangered, since Tisha B'Av is d'rabbanan; and for this matter it applies well to distinguish between d'rabbanan and d'oraisa — between Tisha B'Av and Yom Kippur; not so if we say when they assess her that she will not be endangered it is forbidden even on Tisha B'Av — we have no need to be lenient without assessment, since it can be clarified even on Tisha B'Av to be strict; such appears the intent of the Taz.
yad-ephraim/5:_: In Shulchan Aruch seif 9 — and see below siman 613 where it is explained that it is permitted to wash since one must say "who has formed," see in the Taz.
